 Judgment
By the consent of learned counsel for both the parties, the matter is taken up for final disposal though it is posted for admission and heard the learned counsel appearing for both the sides.

2. This appeal by the petitioner is directed against the judgment and award in MVC No.2087/2015 passed by learned Member, Principal MACT, Bengaluru dated 08.12.2016, whereby, compensation of Rs.15,26,000/- has been awarded.

3. Brief facts that are necessary for the purpose of this appeal are that;
On 03.12.2013 at about 12.30 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding in his car bearing registration No.KA-03/MR-6094 towards Bagepalli on Renugonda Road and near Palasamudram Village, the driver of the lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-26/X-4599 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's vehicle.
As a result, the car was damaged and NC: 2023:KHC:24900 petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was shifted to Jain Hospital, Bengaluru and thereafter, to other Hospitals and he took treatment as inpatient for considerable length of time by spending more than Rs.10,00,000/- and also he had to spend huge amount towards future treatment.

4. Further it was contended that, the petitioner was aged 50 years and he was cultivating his land by growing various vegetables and also he was doing dairy farm having 30 cows and he was earning Rs.75,000/- p.m.
The family members were depending on the income of the petitioner.
Due to the accidental injuries, he has lost his income and also suffering from discomfort to perform his day to day activities and also suffered permanent disability.

It was further contended that the accident in question has occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and the Gorantla Police have registered a case against the driver of the offending vehicle and ultimately,
chargesheeted him.
The respondent No.1 and 2 being the owner and the insurer, are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Therefore, he prayed to award compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/-.

sentences.text: In pursuance of the notice issued by the Tribunal, despite service of notice, the respondents No.1 remained absent and hence, he was placed ex-parte.
The respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement denying all the petition averments.

It has admitted the issuance of policy in respect of the Lorry bearing registration No.AP-26/X-4599 and contended that the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy issued in favour of the owner and in accordance with the provisions of MV Act and also subject to valid and effective driving licence held by the driver of lorry, valid R.C., Permit, F.C.

It was further contended that the driver was not having valid driving licence and the owner/insured has violated the terms and conditions of the policy and hence, it is not liable to indemnify the owner of the insured.

Further, it has disputed the nature of injuries suffered in the accident, the treatment taken in the hospital, the amount spent towards medical expenses on account of accidental injuries and the disabilities suffered by the petitioner and also his earnings and that, the claim of the petitioner is exorbitant and fanciful.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition.
The Tribunal on the basis of the above pleadings, framed appropriate issues.
The petitioner was examined as PW.1, one witness was examined as PW.2 and Exs.P1 to P24 were marked in evidence.
Respondents have not led any evidence.

7. After hearing the arguments, the Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.15,26,000/- under the following heads:
AMOUNT PARTICULARS (IN RS.) Pain and suffering 60,000/- Loss of future earnings due to disability 6,21,000/-

 attendant charges and other incidental 25,000/-
 expenses  Loss of income during the period of  40,000/-
 treatment (Rs.9,000/- x 3)
 Loss of amenities 30,000/-
 TOTAL 15,26,000/-
8. Being aggrieved by the judgment and award, the petitioner has approached this Court in appeal seeking enhancement.

sentences.text: The Tribunal records have been secured and perused the same.

10. The learned counsel appearing for the appellant submits that the Tribunal ought to have assessed the permanent physical disability vis--vis loss of earning capacity at higher than 50% and the Tribunal failed to appreciate the evidence of PW.2 in proper perspective.
The petitioner had suffered quadriparesis on account of the injury to the spinal cord.
Therefore, he submits that the whole body disability as stated by PW.2 to the extent of 78.6% should have been accepted.

He also submits that 'loss of amenities in life' should have been on the higher side considering the fact that the petitioner was unable to walk without support, decreased sensation in all the four limbs.

He also contended that the notional income of the petitioner should have been held higher than Rs.9,000/-
per month as he was an agriculturist cultivating vast extent of the lands.

11. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2 contend that the Tribunal has rightly assessed the disability at 50% and has considered future prospects at 15% in calculating NC:
2023:KHC:24900 the 'loss of future earning'.
He contends that the compensation awarded under other heads is also adequate and there is no need for further enhancement.
12. The petitioner had sustained laceration over the right parietal area of skull, was unable to actively extend the upper limbs and lower limbs and tenderness over the cervical region of the neck.
After diagnostic examination, it was found that there was quadriparesis with C7 compression injury and also was subjected to C7 Laminectomy, decompression of the cord, reduction and posterior fusion.
The discharge summaries produced at Ex.P6, show that he was inpatient in the three spells at VIMS Hospital.
The description of the treatment is narrated by the Tribunal in para 24 of its judgment.
13. The doctor who had examined the petitioner deposed as PW.2 and has narrated the nature of the treatment and the injuries suffered.

In para 36 and 37 of the impugned judgment, the Tribunal states as below:
"a) Right lower limb and left upper limb weakness,
b) Low back pain,
c) Numbness in left upper and lower limbs d) Tightness in abdomen and lower limbs and NC: 2023:KHC:24900 e) Right knee pain

Based on the complaints posed, he noticed the following:
 1) Walking with support  2) Weakness of left shoulder  3) Right him and bilateral toe weakness
4) Decreased sensations in all the four limbs left more than Sri. S. Ravindrakumar vs Sri. K. Parameshwara Reddy on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33455210/

sentences.text: 4  right  5) Spasticity, exaggerated reflexes in right lower limb and  6) Not able to sit squat on the floor, not able to climb stairs  and not able to do his routine works.
37. Upon radiological and clinical examination, he noticed "Pedicle screws from C6 and 2 vertebra with spine alignment maintained"."
14. It is not in dispute that the petitioner was aged 57 years at the time of the accident and he was an agriculturist.
Indisputably the petitioner cannot work as an agriculturist with the above nature of the disabilities.

When we juxtapose the avocation of the petitioner and the nature of the disabilities as observed above, it appears that the functional disability of the petitioner as assessed by the Tribunal at 50% is on the lower side.
PW.2 had stated the disability at 78.6%.
It was a neurological disability resulting in quadriparesis.
However, the cognitive abilities of the petitioner was not impaired.

Hence, in the considered opinion of this Court, the functional disability is 60%.
NC: 2023:KHC:24900 15.
The Tribunal has considered the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.9,000/- per month.

Relying on the decision in the case of SYED SADIQ VS. UNION INDIA INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED1 and the case of the SANJAY KUMAR VS. ASHOK KUMAR2, the Tribunal assessed the loss of future prospects at 15% by considering the age of the petitioner to be 57 years.

sentences.text: Therefore, I do not find any reason to interfere in the said conclusions reached by the Tribunal.
After considering the future prospects at 15%, the Tribunal held the multiplicand to be Rs.11,500/-.
Therefore, 'future loss of income' is calculated as Rs.11,500/- X 12 X 60% X 9 = Rs.7,45,200/- by adopting multiplier of '9' for the age of 57 years.
16. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.60,000/- under the head of 'pain and suffering' which required to be enhanced to Rs.1,00,000/-.
17. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.7,50,000/- towards the 'medical expenses'.
After elaborated discussion, which do not require any interference.

Similarly, the compensation under the head of 'conveyance, food, AIR 2014 SC 1052 2014 ACJ 653 - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:24900 nourishment etc.' at Rs.25,000/- awarded by the Tribunal also do no require any enhancement.
18. The Tribunal has considered the 'loss of income during laid up period' for three months which requires to be enhanced to Rs.60,000/-.
19. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.30,000/- under the head of 'loss of amenities' in life, the petitioner has suffered quadriparesis, which has to suffer for rest of his life.

20. Thus, the petitioner is entitled for the modified compensation under different heads as below:
AMOUNT PARTICULARS (IN RS.)
Pain and suffering 1,00,000/-
Future Loss of income 7,45,200/-

Medical expenses 7,50,000/-
 Conveyance, food and  25,000/-
 nourishment etc  Loss of income during laid up  60,000/-
 period  Loss of amenities in life 75,000/-
 TOTAL 17,55,200/-
Less awarded by Tribunal 15,26,000/-
Enhancement 2,29,200/-
21. Thus, the petitioner is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.2,29,200/- with interest and therefore, the appeal deserves to be allowed in part.

Hence, the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified by awarding a sum of Rs.2,29,200/- in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal together with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its deposit.
(iii) The respondent No.2/Insurance company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of six weeks from the date of this order.
(iv) Rest of the order of the Tribunal stands unaltered.
Sd/-
JUDGE NR/-
